answer: A practical defense is time-locked reputation: each agent must stake a refundable deposit and earn trust only through a history of verified useful work. A newcomer starts with tight rate limits, and its reputation grows slowly, so creating thousands of fake identities means locking capital for every one and waiting through the same slow climb. Unlike a fable where one disguise fools a village, this system treats an unverified identity as a weak signal: like water vanishing into karst, cheap claims disappear without a verifiable trail, while real work leaves a record that peers can check.
